notes: ASSESSABILITY: V02, V11, V09 hardest to judge - fullpage stitches overwhelmingly empty (V11 shows literally nothing below the hero across ~8000px, not even a footer), the pinned-stage signature, so judged largely on hero plus what chrome declares about act structure. Did not treat voids as dead layout, but four of five acts went unverified for V02 and only the overture for V11. FAMILY RESEMBLANCE: NINE OF ELEVEN share a strikingly similar idiom - dark ground, amber/orange accent, fixed bottom transport with SMPTE timecode, five named acts, 'Motion: Full/Reduced' toggle. V01/V02/V04/V05/V07/V08 are the tightest cluster, differing mainly in display face and particle behaviour. V09 is the clear outlier - light, sky-gradient, day-cycle acts - and V11 is the only fully spatial ground-plane treatment. V03 and V10 read as the same idiom attempted with far less control. DEFECT PATTERN: the single most common failure is a fixed header or transport bar with no reserved space or scrim colliding with body text - catastrophic on V06 and V10 mobile, serious on V03 desktop. Second most common is chrome labels clipped by tight containers: V04's III rendering as II, V05's 'WORLD' as 'WOR', V11's track labels, V09's mobile act cells. Confirmed V04 and V05 by zooming; the V09 crop failed so that observation is flagged low-confidence. SCORING NOTE: withheld craft 4 from V07 and V11 despite exceptional rendering - V07 because its desktop breakpoint under-exposes its own headline act, V11 because with essentially no typographic content I could not judge whether type belongs to the same designed language.
